record.paper_title: Local and Global Methods in Data Mining: Basic Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let s be a long string, let σ be a threshold, and for each string w let h(w) denote the number of occurrences of w as a substring of s. If one knows h(w) for every substring w whose count is at least σ, what information about the original string s is determined or recoverable from that thresholded substring-count data?

evidence.quote: Problem 6 Given a long string s and a threshold σ. For a string w, denote by h(w) the number of times w occurs as a substring in s. Suppose we know h(w) for all w such that h(w) ≥ σ. What do we know about the string s?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let s be a finite string over a finite alphabet Σ, and let σ ≥ 1 be an integer threshold. For any string w over Σ, define h(w) to be the number of occurrences of w as a (contiguous) substring of s. Suppose one is given the value h(w) for every string w with h(w) ≥ σ (equivalently, the list of all substrings of s that occur at least σ times in s, each tagged with its multiplicity), but no information about substrings occurring fewer than σ times.

Characterize what can be determined about s from this thresholded substring-frequency data. In particular:
(a) Identify nontrivial invariants of s (such as length, character frequencies, or structural features) that are recoverable from {(w, h(w)) : h(w) ≥ σ}.
(b) Describe equivalence classes of strings that produce identical thresholded data, and give conditions on s and σ (e.g., in terms of the length of s, the alphabet size, or the repetition structure of s) under which s is uniquely determined up to such equivalence.
(c) Provide algorithms, when possible, for reconstructing s (or its equivalence class) from the given data.
artifact.status_search_result: Related problems on string reconstruction from substring compositions, multisets, or spectra have been studied (e.g., unique reconstruction up to reversal for certain lengths, and lower bounds on substring queries by Skiena–Sundaram). However, I could not locate a definitive resolution of this specific thresholded-frequency formulation, where only substrings appearing at least σ times are revealed together with their counts. The status appears to be unknown / open in this exact form.

status_evidence.title: String Reconstruction from Substring Compositions
status_evidence.snippet: Reconstruction of a string from the multiset of its substring compositions; unique up to reversal for certain lengths.
status_evidence.claim: A related but distinct reconstruction setting has partial results, not directly resolving the thresholded-count version.

status_evidence.title: Reconstruction of Strings from their Substrings Spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when the substring spectrum determines the string uniquely.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on substring-spectrum reconstruction; does not settle the thresholded variant.

status_evidence.title: Tight Bounds for String Reconstruction Using Substring Queries
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on the number of substring queries needed to reconstruct a hidden string.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent line of work on query-based reconstruction, not the thresholded-frequency question.
